keywordSourceGroups.summary: .obj只包含纯Mesh数据,顶点，法线，UV,面索引，材质分布。另外有.mtl文件记录材质参数

explanations.text: TRELLIS等系统先生成SDF、Triplane、Sparse Voxel或Structured Latent，再通过iso-surface算法或decoder得到Mesh。可以扩展形状，但拓扑结构可能过于密集或者不太规则。

explanations.text: MeshGPT等系统直接建模triangle或mesh token。可以生成更好的拓扑和更清晰的边缘，但离散连接关系和长token序列更难处理。

sections.heading: 纹理和材质资源
paragraphs: UV贴图、纹素、纹理采样器、mipmap、纹理过滤、法线贴图、置换贴图、纹理压缩、通道打包、材质图、着色器图。

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Texture coordinates map surface samples to texel space; the API specification defines the lookup operation while the normal-map paper shows the mapping used to preserve surface appearance.

details.explanation: A parameterization assigning 2D texture coordinates to points on a 3D surface.
details.aiNote: Neural material systems can compress or infer data related to UV mapping; the renderer still needs predictable random access, filtering, and color semantics.

equation.note: Normalized UV coordinates map into texel coordinates for a W×H texture.

details.explanation: Discrete samples in a texture; they are texture elements, not necessarily one-to-one with screen pixels.
details.aiNote: Neural material systems can compress or infer data related to texels; the renderer still needs predictable random access, filtering, and color semantics.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Williams introduced pyramidal prefiltering to reduce texture minification aliasing; modern sampler state controls reconstruction, minification, addressing, and mip-level selection.

details.explanation: State and hardware logic controlling texture addressing, filtering, mip selection, and comparison behavior.
details.aiNote: Neural material systems can compress or infer data related to texture samplers; the renderer still needs predictable random access, filtering, and color semantics.

details.explanation: A pyramid of prefiltered texture images, each normally half the previous resolution in both dimensions.
details.aiNote: Neural material systems can compress or infer data related to mipmaps; the renderer still needs predictable random access, filtering, and color semantics.

equation.note: ρ is the projected texture footprint scale; larger footprints select coarser levels.

details.explanation: Reconstruction and low-pass filtering used when a projected pixel footprint does not match one texel.
details.aiNote: Neural material systems can compress or infer data related to texture filtering; the renderer still needs predictable random access, filtering, and color semantics.

equation.note: A reconstruction filter combines texel samples with kernel weights.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Appearance-Preserving Simplification stores sampled surface normals in a texture so low-detail geometry can retain high-detail shading.

details.explanation: Textures that store surface-normal directions to reproduce small-scale shading without adding equivalent geometry.
details.aiNote: Neural material systems can compress or infer data related to normal maps; the renderer still needs predictable random access, filtering, and color semantics.

equation.note: The tangent frame transforms a decoded tangent-space normal into world space.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Displacement mapping changes surface position from a map, unlike normal mapping’s shading-only perturbation; MaterialX and the original paper define the offline and interchange forms.

details.explanation: Scalar or vector textures that move surface positions, changing silhouette and geometric intersections.
details.aiNote: Neural material systems can compress or infer data related to displacement maps; the renderer still needs predictable random access, filtering, and color semantics.

equation.note: Scalar displacement d moves the surface along its normal.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Rendering from Compressed Textures establishes block/vector-quantized texture access, while Vulkan defines the compressed formats and sampling behavior used by current GPUs.

details.explanation: GPU-friendly coding of texture blocks or learned features to reduce storage and bandwidth.
details.aiNote: Neural material systems can compress or infer data related to texture compression; the renderer still needs predictable random access, filtering, and color semantics.

equation.note: Bits per pixel/texel is the common storage-rate measure.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Channel packing is an asset convention rather than a standalone rendering algorithm; glTF and MaterialX define which material quantities occupy which texture channels.

details.explanation: Placement of unrelated scalar material maps into separate channels of one texture to reduce fetches and files.
details.aiNote: Neural material systems can compress or infer data related to channel packing; the renderer still needs predictable random access, filtering, and color semantics.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: MaterialX represents connected shading nodes and their typed inputs, providing a portable graph contract rather than tying the graph to one renderer.

details.explanation: Node networks that describe reusable material computations and connect parameters, textures, and scattering models.
details.aiNote: Neural material systems can compress or infer data related to material graphs; the renderer still needs predictable random access, filtering, and color semantics.

details.explanation: Visual or serialized graphs compiled into executable shader code for one or more pipeline stages.
details.aiNote: Neural material systems can compress or infer data related to shader graphs; the renderer still needs predictable random access, filtering, and color semantics.

aiResearch.summary: Neural texture compression and neural appearance models learn compact texture and material representations that can be decoded inside rendering workloads.

sections.heading: Large-world and terrain representation
paragraphs: Heightfield, heightmap, weightmap, terrain tiles, quadtree, geometry clipmaps, continuous geo-mipmapping, LOD, HLOD, world partition, geometry streaming, virtual texturing, runtime virtual textures.
Modern large-world systems combine geometry LOD with streaming and partitioning. [Unreal Engine Landscape overview](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/landscape-overview)

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Heightfield terrain is sampled into nested spatial tiles; geometry-clipmap research and the implementation chapter explain the regular grids and hierarchical updates.

details.explanation: A surface represented by one height value h(x,z) over each horizontal location, so it cannot represent overhangs directly.
details.aiNote: Diffusion terrain systems can generate Heightfield data, but seamless boundaries, scale, editability, and runtime streaming remain explicit engineering constraints.

equation.note: A heightfield has one elevation for each horizontal coordinate.

details.explanation: An image or grid whose sample values encode terrain or surface elevation.
details.aiNote: Diffusion terrain systems can generate heightmap data, but seamless boundaries, scale, editability, and runtime streaming remain explicit engineering constraints.

details.explanation: A texture of blending weights, commonly used to mix terrain materials or procedural layers.
details.aiNote: Diffusion terrain systems can generate weightmap data, but seamless boundaries, scale, editability, and runtime streaming remain explicit engineering constraints.

details.explanation: Spatial chunks of terrain data loaded, culled, and refined independently.
details.aiNote: Diffusion terrain systems can generate terrain tiles data, but seamless boundaries, scale, editability, and runtime streaming remain explicit engineering constraints.

details.explanation: A hierarchy that recursively subdivides a 2D region into four children for culling, LOD, or streaming.
details.aiNote: Diffusion terrain systems can generate quadtree data, but seamless boundaries, scale, editability, and runtime streaming remain explicit engineering constraints.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Geometry clipmaps maintain nested, view-centered resolution levels and update them incrementally to provide continuous terrain LOD.

details.explanation: Nested, camera-centered regular grids that update incrementally to render large heightfields at multiple resolutions.
details.aiNote: Diffusion terrain systems can generate geometry clipmaps data, but seamless boundaries, scale, editability, and runtime streaming remain explicit engineering constraints.

details.explanation: Terrain LOD that interpolates or morphs between grid resolutions to hide discrete switching.
details.aiNote: Diffusion terrain systems can generate continuous geo-mipmapping data, but seamless boundaries, scale, editability, and runtime streaming remain explicit engineering constraints.

details.explanation: Level of detail: selection of a cheaper representation when projected error is sufficiently small.
details.aiNote: Diffusion terrain systems can generate LOD data, but seamless boundaries, scale, editability, and runtime streaming remain explicit engineering constraints.

equation.note: Projected error decreases with depth z and increases with focal scale f.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: World Partition divides a large world into streamable cells, while HLOD replaces distant groups with simplified proxies.

details.explanation: Hierarchical level of detail: replacement of groups of objects with combined proxies at distance.
details.aiNote: Diffusion terrain systems can generate HLOD data, but seamless boundaries, scale, editability, and runtime streaming remain explicit engineering constraints.

details.explanation: Division of a large world into independently streamable cells managed by spatial position and runtime relevance.
details.aiNote: Diffusion terrain systems can generate world partition data, but seamless boundaries, scale, editability, and runtime streaming remain explicit engineering constraints.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Progressive meshes formalize continuous-resolution transmission, and current World Partition documentation shows the production streaming counterpart.

details.explanation: Loading and evicting geometric pages or clusters according to visibility, distance, and memory budget.
details.aiNote: Diffusion terrain systems can generate geometry streaming data, but seamless boundaries, scale, editability, and runtime streaming remain explicit engineering constraints.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Virtual texturing pages texture data on demand; Unreal’s documentation distinguishes streamed virtual textures from runtime-generated virtual-texture caches.

details.explanation: A large logical texture backed by smaller physical pages that are loaded only when sampled.
details.aiNote: Diffusion terrain systems can generate virtual texturing data, but seamless boundaries, scale, editability, and runtime streaming remain explicit engineering constraints.

details.explanation: Virtual textures rendered from scene data during execution and reused by later shading passes.
details.aiNote: Diffusion terrain systems can generate runtime virtual textures data, but seamless boundaries, scale, editability, and runtime streaming remain explicit engineering constraints.

aiResearch.summary: Diffusion models are being applied to terrain heightfields, textures, and large procedural worlds, with continuity and editability becoming central research constraints.

sections.heading: Modern alternative scene representations
paragraphs: Point cloud, voxel, signed distance field, surfel, neural radiance field, NeRF, radiance field, 3D Gaussian Splatting, splat rasterization, differentiable rendering, novel-view synthesis.

3DGS should be presented as a learned scene representation and visibility-aware splatting method, not as an ordinary mesh file format. [Original 3D Gaussian Splatting paper](https://doi.org/10.1145/3592433)

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Point-based graphics treats oriented samples or surfels as renderable surface elements; PCL and Open3D document the point-cloud data and processing side.

details.explanation: An unordered or weakly structured set of 3D samples, often carrying color, normal, or confidence attributes.
details.aiNote: Point cloud is directly relevant to neural scene representations: current work optimizes learned primitives for reconstruction, generation, and differentiable rendering.

details.explanation: An oriented surface element with position, normal, radius, and appearance rather than explicit triangle connectivity.
details.aiNote: surfel is directly relevant to neural scene representations: current work optimizes learned primitives for reconstruction, generation, and differentiable rendering.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Voxels discretize a field in space, while signed-distance fields store distance and sign; OpenVDB supplies sparse storage and sphere tracing supplies the canonical SDF intersection method.

details.explanation: A sample or cell in a three-dimensional grid representing density, occupancy, material, or another volumetric field.
details.aiNote: voxel is directly relevant to neural scene representations: current work optimizes learned primitives for reconstruction, generation, and differentiable rendering.

details.explanation: A scalar field giving distance to the nearest surface, with sign distinguishing inside from outside.
details.aiNote: signed distance field is directly relevant to neural scene representations: current work optimizes learned primitives for reconstruction, generation, and differentiable rendering.

equation.note: The sign classifies inside/outside while magnitude is nearest-surface distance.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: NeRF learns a continuous density-and-radiance field from images and renders new views by integrating that field along camera rays.

details.explanation: A learned continuous function that maps position and view direction to density and emitted radiance.
details.aiNote: neural radiance field is directly relevant to neural scene representations: current work optimizes learned primitives for reconstruction, generation, and differentiable rendering.

equation.note: NeRF integrates learned density and view-dependent color along a ray.

details.explanation: The canonical neural radiance-field method trained from posed images and rendered by integrating samples along rays.
details.aiNote: NeRF is directly relevant to neural scene representations: current work optimizes learned primitives for reconstruction, generation, and differentiable rendering.

equation.note: Transmittance weights how much radiance survives before a sample.

details.explanation: A spatial-directional function describing the radiance traveling through each point in each direction.
details.aiNote: radiance field is directly relevant to neural scene representations: current work optimizes learned primitives for reconstruction, generation, and differentiable rendering.

details.explanation: Rendering viewpoints not present in the input observations while preserving scene consistency.
details.aiNote: novel-view synthesis is directly relevant to neural scene representations: current work optimizes learned primitives for reconstruction, generation, and differentiable rendering.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting optimizes anisotropic Gaussian primitives and projects them with visibility-aware splat rasterization for real-time novel views.

details.explanation: An explicit radiance-field representation made of anisotropic 3D Gaussians projected and alpha-composited as splats.
details.aiNote: 3D Gaussian Splatting is directly relevant to neural scene representations: current work optimizes learned primitives for reconstruction, generation, and differentiable rendering.

equation.note: Each primitive is centered at μ with anisotropic covariance Σ.

details.explanation: Projection of finite point kernels into screen footprints that are accumulated rather than assembled as triangles.
details.aiNote: splat rasterization is directly relevant to neural scene representations: current work optimizes learned primitives for reconstruction, generation, and differentiable rendering.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Differentiable rendering exposes image derivatives with respect to scene parameters; the survey, Mitsuba 2 paper, and Mitsuba 3 documentation cover the concept and a working system.

details.explanation: Rendering that also computes image derivatives with respect to geometry, materials, lights, or camera parameters.
details.aiNote: differentiable rendering is directly relevant to neural scene representations: current work optimizes learned primitives for reconstruction, generation, and differentiable rendering.

aiResearch.summary: Neural fields, Gaussian splats, and unified differentiable primitives remain a fast-moving alternative to fixed meshes, especially for reconstruction and generative 3D.

sections.heading: Coordinate spaces
paragraphs: Object space, local space, world space, view space, eye space, clip space, normalized device coordinates, NDC, screen space, viewport space, framebuffer coordinates.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: These coordinate spaces are related by object-to-world and world-to-camera transforms; PBRT and Direct3D document the same transformation chain with different conventions.

details.explanation: The coordinate system attached to one object's authored geometry before placement in the scene.
details.aiNote: There is no separate AI definition of Object space; differentiable renderers use the same coordinate contract while learning adjacent scene parameters.

equation.note: The model transform places object coordinates into the world.

details.explanation: A coordinate system defined relative to a parent object, node, bone, or procedural frame.
details.aiNote: There is no separate AI definition of local space; differentiable renderers use the same coordinate contract while learning adjacent scene parameters.

equation.note: A local transform expresses a child relative to its parent.

details.explanation: The shared scene coordinate system after object and hierarchy transforms are applied.
details.aiNote: There is no separate AI definition of world space; differentiable renderers use the same coordinate contract while learning adjacent scene parameters.

equation.note: The view matrix changes the basis from world to camera.

details.explanation: Coordinates expressed relative to the camera after applying the view transform.
details.aiNote: There is no separate AI definition of view space; differentiable renderers use the same coordinate contract while learning adjacent scene parameters.

equation.note: Projection maps camera-space coordinates into clip space.

details.explanation: Another name for view or camera space in many graphics APIs and texts.
details.aiNote: There is no separate AI definition of eye space; differentiable renderers use the same coordinate contract while learning adjacent scene parameters.

equation.note: Eye space is transformed by the projection matrix.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: Clip coordinates are produced before homogeneous division; Vulkan then defines the normalized-device coordinate volume and clipping rules.

details.explanation: Homogeneous coordinates after projection but before division by w and viewport mapping.
details.aiNote: There is no separate AI definition of clip space; differentiable renderers use the same coordinate contract while learning adjacent scene parameters.

equation.note: Homogeneous division produces normalized device coordinates.

details.explanation: Post-divide canonical coordinates inside the API's normalized clipping volume.
details.aiNote: There is no separate AI definition of normalized device coordinates; differentiable renderers use the same coordinate contract while learning adjacent scene parameters.

equation.note: NDC follows the perspective divide.

details.explanation: Abbreviation for normalized device coordinates.
details.aiNote: There is no separate AI definition of NDC; differentiable renderers use the same coordinate contract while learning adjacent scene parameters.

equation.note: NDC is the post-divide canonical space.

keywordSourceGroups.summary: The viewport maps normalized device coordinates into framebuffer coordinates, after which screen-space tests and raster operations address samples.

details.explanation: Coordinates or operations expressed over the projected image domain.
details.aiNote: There is no separate AI definition of screen space; differentiable renderers use the same coordinate contract while learning adjacent scene parameters.

details.explanation: Coordinates after the viewport scale and offset map NDC into a target rectangle.
details.aiNote: There is no separate AI definition of viewport space; differentiable renderers use the same coordinate contract while learning adjacent scene parameters.

equation.note: The viewport scales and offsets NDC into the target rectangle.

details.explanation: Discrete or continuous coordinates addressing framebuffer pixels and samples.
details.aiNote: There is no separate AI definition of framebuffer coordinates; differentiable renderers use the same coordinate contract while learning adjacent scene parameters.

equation.note: Rasterization maps continuous positions to discrete sample locations.

aiResearch.summary: There is no AI-specific replacement for coordinate spaces. Differentiable renderers keep the same transforms and optimize the camera, geometry, or appearance parameters that flow through them.

details.explanation: The angular extent visible through the camera, normally specified vertically or horizontally.
details.aiNote: AI can estimate or optimize parameters affecting field of view, but projection and camera geometry remain the physical image-formation model.
